name: NJ-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Herb Conaway holds a lopsided money edge; Republican Michael McGuire reports about $800 on hand
District leans Democratic (D+5) and the national environment favors Democrats this cycle
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%
No public polling in the district, so the rating rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Conaway's incumbency, a D+5 district, a favorable environment, and a huge fundraising gap over an opponent with under $1,000 in the bank all point the same direction, and markets agree at roughly 98%. With no polling available, uncertainty stays wide, but the safe-Democratic rating stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or a surge of outside spending behind McGuire would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Herb Conaway, the Democratic incumbent, seeks a full term in a New Jersey district that leans Democratic by about five points. He enters the general election with a decisive financial edge: roughly $935,000 raised and $439,000 on hand, while Republican Michael McGuire has raised under $80,000 and reports just $807 in cash. No outside groups are spending against Conaway, and the minor-party candidates on the ballot lack visible funding.

Public polling is absent, so the assessment rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near 98%. The national environment also favors Democrats this cycle. Together these point to a comfortable incumbent win, with the main caveat being the lack of direct polling in the district.
